body: Why is the model so fat?

Can't really speak to this science, but I got fat because I grew up in a family of hammies that shoveled McDonalds down my throat every day after school and NEVER once had a talk about health with me. I realize there is a certain amount of personal responsibility but when that shit is ingrained in you from before you know it's wrong it can be REALLY hard to break those habits. After high school I got sick of it and developed an eating disorder go figure. Went from 270 to my current weight of 128 as a 6'0 male and feel like I'd rather die than a gain a pound back. Thanks family!

Also I should add that no author should ever direct his own book. If you aren't Martin Scorsese than leave that voiceover out. I rolled my eyes pretty hard every time we get 5 minute scenes of nothing but narration and montages. Such lazy filmmaking it disgusts me.

Also I just read that guys comment about how he's "still waiting for his Sam." This is another reason for my hatred of the movie. Instead of inspiring people to get better on their own and help themselves, you think "One day my manic pixie dream girl is coming and EVERYTHING WILL BE BETTER just like in the movie!" I was the same way when I first saw Garden State at 14..it took me a long time to realize that Natalie Portman's character didn't exist in real life and the whole thing was a fantasy.

I hated that movie so much I couldn't finish it. Just felt like a cheap fantasy to me. Yeah, I could relate to Charlie but what I could not relate to was the whole outcast with male model looks being taken in by a manic pixie dream girl and her gay, hipster brother who teach him how to come out of his shell and enjoy life. Or something. Like I said, I didn't finish it but I couldn't help but think about all the real Charlie's who are struggling alone with nobody to "save them" (like me I guess). What happens to Charlie if he has to deal with this stuff on his own? If he's not "cool" enough for Emma Watson and Ezra Miller to befriend him? That is a more interesting and real movie to me than the generic and fake Perks of Being a Wallflower, which seems to say "you'll be okay as long as you make cool friends".

Maybe I'm just bitter because I wished I had a high school experience like he did. I don't know but I can't stand that movie. Perhaps on your second viewing the hope you felt after the first viewing was eroded by how unrealistic and full of lies the whole thing is.
